title: When gripping starts pretending to be care
issueStatement: The mind keeps tightening around outcomes because uncertainty feels unbearable, and the grip starts calling itself responsibility.
centralInsight: Guru separates response from authorship. Control weakens when the heart remembers it was never asked to be the maker of every result.
practicalReflection: The controlling mind grows tired because it treats every outcome as personal territory. Release becomes possible when peace no longer depends on total command.
actionPrompt: Release one demand that peace must wait for a guaranteed result, and answer the situation you actually have.

practice.label: Steady Practice
practice.title: When control needs a repeatable shape
practice.issueStatement: The mind keeps gripping outcomes because uncertainty feels like exposure. What is needed now is not another insight about surrender but a practiced interruption that reaches the body before control gets fluent.
practice.centralInsight: The grip has its own liturgy: refresh, re-check, rehearse, press harder. Guru breaks it by restoring creatureliness: answer cleanly, but stop pretending you are the keeper of outcomes.
practice.practicalReflection: A real rule catches control at the first bodily theft, the hand closing, the jaw setting, the second message forming. If the practice starts later than that, the room is already being managed.
practice.actionPrompt: Choose one cue all week, the refresh, the threshold, or the second follow-up. At that cue, open the hand, soften the jaw, and answer only what is actually yours.
